subject: BrightLayer: AWS Marketplace metering & SaaS fulfillment — integration questions
messages:
From: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@brightlayer.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLayer / Redwood — AWS Marketplace metering questions

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. We want to get the AWS Marketplace path configured so our customers are billed via the Marketplace and we can reconcile entitlements on our side. Quick summary of what BrightLayer needs to confirm before procurement signs: 

- Confirm metering dimension(s): per-concurrent-seat vs. consumption (tokens/requests).
- Entitlement mapping: how SaaS contract seats map to AWS entitlements for seat-based enrollments.
- Invoice flow & settlement timing (BrightLayer needs 30-day net close).
- Any required changes to our SaaS contract SOW for marketplace listing (Doc attached).

I'm attaching a redacted copy of our SaaS contract and a short diagram of our internal seat registry. Can you share the entitlement schema you expect and the minimum events we need to emit to Marketplace?

Appreciate a short checklist we can share with procurement.

Best,
Jordan Cole
Head of Cloud Partnerships
BrightLayer Analytics

Attachments: BrightLayer_SaaS_Contract_redacted.pdf, seat_registry_diagram.png

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@brightlayer.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLayer / Redwood — AWS Marketplace metering questions

Jordan — thanks for the clear list and the contract. Looping in Aditya (sales lead) and Laura (finance) so we have procurement and billing visibility; Dev from infra will confirm any technical constraints.

High-level answers and asks from our side:

- Metering model: We support both seat and consumption models on our AWS listing. For seat-based we use an entitlement ID per customer and an activation event. For consumption we accept periodic metering records (hourly/daily) that map to your account id.

- Entitlement mapping: Please send your internal seat ID format (example you attached helps). We'll provide an entitlement schema (attached) — include fields: customer_external_id, entitlement_id, start_ts, end_ts, units.

- Required events: activation, deactivation, and consumption_batch (timestamped with units). Minimum real-time footprint: activation/deactivation within 5 minutes of change for seat models, consumption batched hourly for usage.

- SOW changes: We typically add an appendix describing entitlement granularity and the reconciliation cadence. Laura — can you confirm whether a 30-day settlement request affects invoicing?

Next steps: I attached our aws_entitlement_schema_v1.pdf. Can BrightLayer: 1) confirm sample payloads for activation & consumption; 2) confirm whether procurement wants us to push a subscription amendment or if they'll sign via DocuSign final SOW? If you prefer, we can draft the Marketplace appendix and send to procurement for review.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Tel: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: aws_entitlement_schema_v1.pdf

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@brightlayer.ai>, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 6 Sep 2025 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLayer / Redwood — AWS Marketplace metering questions

Jordan + team — thanks, this is actionable. Below is a short mutual action plan (MAP) so procurement has clear milestones.

MAP:
1) BrightLayer: Send two sample payloads (activation + consumption_batch) and one sample mapping table for historical seat changes — due: Tue 9 Sep.
2) Redwood: Provide appendix language for the Marketplace SOW and confirm expected settlement delays for both seat and consumption billing models — due: Wed 10 Sep.
3) BrightLayer procurement: Confirm preferred signing path (DocuSign powerform vs. amendment) and any legal redlines — due: Fri 12 Sep.
4) Joint: End-to-end sandbox test (provisioning → entitlement activation → metering event → AWS billing test) — target: week of Sep 22.

Technical note (Dev): Dev, can you confirm whether we should recommend hourly consumption batches or if daily is sufficient to keep costs predictable for BrightLayer's customers? If customers need near-real-time seat activation, we can recommend webhook for activation events.

Jordan — I'll draft the appendix and attach a short SOW outline. Laura, if 30-day settlement is a requirement, flag any billing ops callbacks that require accounting changes.

Thanks — Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Procurement <procurement@procure.brightlayer.ai>

From: Procurement <procurement@procure.brightlayer.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: SOW & DocuSign request — Redwood AWS Marketplace listing
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Camila — thanks for the entitlement schema. Procurement has reviewed and requests the following small amendments to the appendix:

- Explicit reconciliation window: monthly reconciliations with a 7-day dispute window.
- Final settlement: BrightLayer requires 30-day net settlement; Redwood to confirm whether Marketplace timing introduces an extra 14-day delay to vendor payouts.
- Audit logs: BrightLayer requires a 12-month retention of metering event logs and CSV export on demand.

We are OK to sign the SOW once the appendix includes the reconciliation clause and a clear note on expected payout timing. Please send the DocuSign link for the final SOW and we will route for approval today.

Forwarding our approval to proceed with sandbox testing pending the SOW changes. Attaching procurement checklist (internal).

Procurement
BrightLayer Analytics

Attachments referenced: procurement_checklist.pdf

DocuSign link (powerform): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=demo&id=ABC123

Regards,
